doc.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018

title: His daughters, sons-in-law and grandchildren
summary: His five daughters wouldn't marry musicians; he is proud of their marriages and family.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: I just have this picture of you telling your grandkids, “You hear that song? I’m playing on that.” “Sure, Grandpa.”

That would happen every now and then. When — my kids too because they know pretty much about my career but I have five daughters. Neither of them would marry a musician, ever. Which is amusing to me. But they can see how sporadic that kind of lifestyle could be, and they all married men, I mean I’m proud of all my sons-in-laws, great people. And at least I feel that one of my objectives, and I’ve talked with them a lot

about that, was to give them the judgement to choose a mate that would not be abusive or was not an evil person basically. And they all made me proud in their choices. They’ve stayed with their spouses, each one of them. And I actually have now five great- grandchildren.
Wow. You know bless your heart. You’re 83 now?
